prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
The API now requires a key on every request, enforces the three roles, and audits changing requests, with `GET /audit` for managers only. `npm test` (26 pass) and `npm run lint` pass; I checked the 401/403 and role behaviour with a throwaway script, and added no new tests since the task only asked to update existing ones.

One thing to act on: `data/db.json` (the default file for `npm start`) has no keys, so the server answers 401 to everything until you add `apiKeys` entries to it. I left it alone because you only named `data/seed.json` and I did not want to put sample keys into live data.

- **Keys:** `data/seed.json` has `seed-viewer-key`, `seed-cook-key` and `seed-manager-key`.
- **Roles:** cook may additionally use `POST /recipes/:id/cook`, `POST /batches/:id/waste`, `POST /temperatures` and `POST /stocktakes/:id/counts`. Starting and finishing a stock-take stay manager-only, as does every other non-GET route.
- **Errors:** new codes `unauthorized` (401) and `forbidden` (403), with English and Korean messages. A missing or unknown key gets 401 even on routes that do not exist.
- **Audit:** every non-GET request from a known key is recorded with its status, including refused (403) and failed ones. Requests answered 401 are not recorded, since there is no key name and anyone could otherwise grow the file.
- **Schema:** bumped to 3 with a migration that adds empty `apiKeys` and `audit`. That forced a change to `tests/cli.test.js` beyond sending a key: it now expects `schema 1 → 3`.
- **Tests:** `tests/helpers.js` sends the manager key by default, so the individual test files are unchanged.
- **Saves:** an audited request now writes the data file twice, once by the route and once for the audit entry.

check.why: keys, roles, audit and docs all right
